mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of each proposed director, officer, subscriber and ultimate beneficial owner's valid passport
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority and a notary public in the document's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the origin country is a party to the 1961 Apostille Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization through the Canadian embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-state corporate registry or the corporate secretary of the shareholder entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Hague jurisdictions, legalization by the relevant Canadian diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized bank reference letter confirming source of funds and factual beneficial ownership of the proposed funding institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Authorized financial institution maintaining the funding account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable to the banking document

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders holding 25% or more, and all ultimate beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List where relevant, Global Affairs Canada sanctions registered under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, the RCMP-CCIRC advisories, and reputable commercial PEP and adverse-media databases (e.g. World-Check or LexisNexis). Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, any country listed by FATF as having strategic AML/CFT deficiencies, and any unusual source-of-funds pattern. All screening results must be dated, retained for at least five years, and made available to FINTRAC, Revenu Quebec, or other competent authorities upon request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - Registre des entreprises du Quebec online portal (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca/)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate legal name must contain a French legal element or a French-language variant acceptable under the Quebec Business Corporations Act and must comply with the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11). Names may be composed of words in French, English or another language, but the compulsory legal or descriptive element must be expressed in French, including the statutory abbreviations 'inc.', 'corp.', 'ltée' or the explicit French 'société par actions' where applicable. Non-Latin characters are not accepted in the legal name; any foreign-language corporate or trademark element must be furnished in a Latin-alphabet transliteration. The name must not be misleading, contrary to public order, or confusingly similar to any existing name, trademark or legal person recorded in the Quebec enterprise register.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must file a written request for reconsideration with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec within 30 days of the refusal notice, appending a revised proposed name and any additional supporting trademark or consent documents. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may appeal to the Tribunal administratif du Quebec within 60 days of the reconsideration decision, in accordance with the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. An external, licensed name-search provider may be used to obtain a pre-clearance opinion before filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual mail-forwarding-only address is not acceptable as the sole registered or head office under Quebec law; the registered office must be a physical location in Quebec where service of process can be made and where the statutory records can be produced. A licensed registered-office service provider offering a physical reception, meeting room access and named agent service may be used for administrative and compliance purposes, but the corporation must maintain either its principal establishment or an agent in Quebec at a verifiable physical address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: less than 5% likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection during the first 12 months for a standard low-risk wholesale import/export business, provided no AML trigger, insolvency proceeding, customs complaint, or tax-administration flag is raised by Revenu Quebec, Canada Revenue Agency or the Canada Border Services Agency.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA) / Loi sur les sociétés par actions, CQLR c. S-31.1, Part II (Incorporation and Organization), arts. 5 et seq. (articles of incorporation and certificate), registered office provisions, and first directors and organizational meeting provisions; federal alternative: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 5-13
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Quebec Enterprise Registrar (for provincial incorporation under QBCA); Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (for federal CBCA route)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation / Statuts de constitution (QBCA Form), filed electronically with REQ
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the QBCA; no escrow or trust account is required at incorporation. The authorized share structure (one or more classes) is declared in the Articles, and shares may be issued for such minimum consideration as the incorporator or Board fixes, subject to the corporate solvency test. Authorized capital may be set at zero par value with issuance for CAD 0.01 per share or nominal subscribed capital; full payment may be deferred to a Board call.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Resolved that the Corporation's Articles be and are hereby confirmed; that the subscription of one common share by the incorporator be and is hereby accepted, the consideration fixed in accordance with the Articles, and a share certificate issued; that the registered office be and is hereby established at a designated address in the Province of Quebec, and the Registraire des entreprises and any other governing registry be notified; that the corporate bank account be opened with signatory authorities as instrumented; that one or more named individuals act as director(s), President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each to serve until the next shareholders' meeting; and that management be authorized to execute all ancillary filings, declarations, and licences.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Corporate Name Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) online name-services portal; Corporations Canada NUANS system for the federal route
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a NUANS name search request electronically and obtain the name search report. The proposed legal name must include distinctive, descriptive, and legal elements and must comply with the Charter of the French Language (French-language version mandatory). Upon a clear report, reserve the name for up to 90 days and use the reservation reference when preparing the Articles of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Completed NUANS name search request form
Proposed corporate name in French (mandatory) with optional English version
Written consent of any person whose name is used, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity or violation of the French-language rules, file a revised NUANS request with a new distinctive element, or submit a written consent from the conflicting name holder; REQ will re-issue a reservation without an additional filing fee for the same application batch within the statutory review period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Filing of Statutory Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online sociétés par actions incorporation service (Corporations Canada if federal CBCA chosen)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation (statuts de constitution) in French or bilingual form, specifying the authorized share structure, share class rights and restrictions, any restrictions on transfer, and the initial directors. Submit the electronic filing to REQ and pay the incorporation fee. Upon approval, REQ issues the Certificate of Incorporation and simultaneously publishes the registration in the Registre des entreprises.
required_dossiers: Declared registered office address in Quebec
Names and residential addresses of the incorporator and initial directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a notice of deficiency or non-compliance under the QBCA, cure by filing corrective articles through the online amendment service within 30 days; once corrected, the certificate is issued with effect from the original submission date where the cure is administrative only.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirmation of Public Registry Entry and Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — public registry and attestation services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon incorporation, verify the REQ public registry extract, confirm the NEQ, and validate the published information on the registered office, directors, and object. If a federal CBCA corporation was chosen instead, register the corporation as an extra-provincial company with REQ and obtain the NEQ. Thereafter, file the annual declaration (déclaration de mise à jour) to keep the registry record current.
required_dossiers: Initial notice of registered office and board of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry extraction contains errors, file an online rectification with REQ; if the enterprise status is struck or dissolved for failure to file the annual declaration, cure by filing the outstanding declaration with late penalty and, if necessary, applying for revival under the QBCA within the statutory limitation period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Governance — First Board Resolution, By-Laws, and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's Board of Directors; filings to REQ (notice of directors) and financial institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first organizational board meeting and adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution covering share subscription, registered office, and officer appointments. Approve the by-laws, issue share certificates, enter them in the securities register, open the corporate bank account, and file the notice of registered office and directors with REQ within 20 days after incorporation.
required_dossiers: Share subscription agreement and securities register
Notice of registered office and board of directors (REQ Form)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ rejects the notice of directors due to signature or content defects, correct and resubmit the notice form; the bank may likewise require a certified copy of the corrected resolution, which is obtainable by a ministerial meeting of the Board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA and Revenu Québec Tax Registration and Business Number Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online; Revenu Québec — mandatory online business registration (MOB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation with the CRA for a 9-digit federal Business Number and activate the corporate income tax account, GST/HST account (once taxable supplies exceed the CAD 30,000 threshold or voluntarily), payroll deductions account if employees are hired, and import/export account if applicable. Separately register with Revenu Québec for the Québec Sales Tax (TVQ), Québec corporate income tax, and employer source-deduction accounts. Maintain tax records as required by the Taxation Act and the Excise Tax Act.
required_dossiers: Registered office address and proof of address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or Revenu Québec queries the registration due to unverified corporate status, resubmit the attestation and NEQ; discrepancies in account setup are cured by amending the Business Number registration online in My Business Account or through Revenu Québec's client service portal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation du Québec (MAPAQ) — Food Establishment Permit Service; municipal permit office of the local Quebec municipality; Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) for federal food safety and export requirements
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Establishment Permit (Permis d'établissement alimentaire) under the Food Products Act (Loi sur les produits alimentaires), CQLR c. P-29 and its regulations; municipal commercial operating permit; CFIA Safe Food for Canadians Act licence for interprovincial and international trade in food commodities

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement et de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / attestation category: dry-storage, re-packing, and wholesale of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals is below the threshold requiring a Full EIA Report; an environmental compliance registration or attestation is required where warehouse expansion, wastewater discharge, or cold-storage mechanical systems are installed, subject to municipal and provincial by-laws.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater expected from dry botanical handling; any sanitary discharge must meet municipal sewer-use limits (e.g., Montreal by-law 2008-47 or local municipality thresholds for BOD, TSS, and pH); VOC and dust emissions must remain below the Clean Air Regulation (RLRQ c. Q-2, r. 4.1) limits; food-contact hygiene and pest control must comply with CFIA Safe Food for Canadians Regulations; organic certification and allergen cross-contamination controls per Codex Alimentarius where applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Building Code and Fire Safety Act (Loi sur la sécurité incendie), including municipal fire inspection and emergency exit plan; structural load inspection for warehouse racking systems; workplace health and safety registration with CNESST, including prevention program, equipment compliance, and occupational hygiene; municipal electrical, plumbing, and occupancy permits; employee health clearance and WHMIS training where chemicals are stored.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA) — federal corporate income tax, GST/HST, and Business Number (BN) administration via the My Business Account portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html); Revenu Québec — Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and Quebec corporate income tax schedules, portal https://www.revenuquebec.ca; Registraire des entreprises du Québec — issuance of the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), portal https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident-owned Quebec Business Corporation: (1) incorporate federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act or provincially under the Quebec Business Corporations Act (or both), and obtain the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; (2) if federally incorporated, complete extra-provincial registration with the Registraire des entreprises when the registered office or a place of business is located in Quebec; (3) obtain the 9-digit CRA Business Number (BN) by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or via the CRA Business Registration Online service — non-residents with Canadian nexus may use Form RC4020 and must appoint a representative for service; (4) activate the GST/HST account (RT), the corporate tax program account (RC), and any import/export account (RM); (5) register the QST account (RD program) with Revenu Québec once taxable supplies are made in Quebec; (6) retain the certificate of incorporation, articles, NEQ confirmation, BN, and QST registration in the statutory corporate file.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a Canadian Business Corporation is a per se taxable person under the Income Tax Act and may not elect pass-through treatment; resident corporations are taxable on worldwide income, while the territorial scope for non-resident corporations limits Canadian tax to Canadian-source income (subject to treaty relief). Quebec levies a separate provincial corporate income tax on income allocable to Quebec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box classification election; corporate status is statutory. Relevant elections include: subsection 85(1) Income Tax Act rollover election on incorporation or asset transfers; section 156 Excise Tax Act election for closely related corporations to treat taxable supplies as made for nominal consideration for GST/HST; early GST/HST registration election for small suppliers under section 233 of the Excise Tax Act; the associated-enterprise QST election under section 21 of the Act respecting the Quebec sales tax; and the hybrid-mismatch deduction restrictions under sections 18.4–18.6 Income Tax Act, under which Canada applies structured-arrangement rules rather than elective relief for hybrid mismatch outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) — federal VAT-type consumption tax at 5% in Quebec, plus the separate Quebec Sales Tax (QST) at 9.975% administered by Revenu Québec; both are invoice-credit VAT systems and exports are zero-rated.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 — the small supplier threshold for GST/HST is based on the value of worldwide taxable supplies made in Canada (including zero-rated exports) in the current calendar quarter or the immediately preceding four calendar quarters; the QST threshold is C$30,000 of taxable supplies made in Quebec over the same look-back periods. This bulk exporter's export revenues count toward the threshold, making GST/HST and QST registration mandatory once C$30,000 is exceeded; voluntary registration is available below the threshold to claim input tax credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, API-based clearance, or digital stamping for GST/HST or QST. The CRA and Revenu Québec accept paper and electronic invoices (PDF, EDI, XML) that comply with section 223 of the Excise Tax Act and the equivalent QST invoicing provisions; the Pan-Canadian Peppol e-invoice network is voluntary at this stage. Export sellers must retain the original invoice, export declaration, and carrier documentation in readable electronic form to substantiate zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act: (i) goods exported by the registrant supplier to a non-resident consignee outside Canada (section 1); and (ii) services supplied to non-residents, including logistics and preparation services directly related to the exported goods (section 7). The dried goji berry and herbal botanical exports qualify when legal ownership passes to the non-resident buyer, the goods are shipped directly from Quebec to a foreign destination, and the exporter maintains the prescribed documentary evidence. The registrant may also claim input tax credits (refunds) for GST/HST and QST paid on related inputs, subject to the same substantiation standard.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (B13A) or CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System (CESR) electronic transmission (G13 form) completed by the exporter or licensed customs broker
Commercial invoice with full botanical description, HS classification (HS 0813 for dried goji berries / HS 1211 for herbal botanicals), quantity, unit value, Incoterms, and foreign destination
Bill of lading (ocean, air, or truck) or other contract of carriage proving departure from Canada and arrival at a foreign destination
Inward remittance certificate, SWIFT MT103 wire-transfer record, or bank credit advice evidencing settlement by the non-resident buyer
Packing list and certificate of origin for the herbal consignment
GST/HST and QST export ledger reconciliation, CRA export sales listing, and retained input tax credit notes
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec auditors reverse zero-rating where the export documentation bundle is incomplete or untimely, assessing GST/HST and QST on the full invoice value with arrears interest under the Excise Tax Act and section 285 gross-negligence penalties (up to 25% of the understated tax or a C$250 minimum, whichever is greater). Deliberate false claims attract criminal prosecution under section 327 of the Excise Tax Act and section 380 of the Criminal Code, plus revocation of GST/HST registration under section 241. CRA may also impose transfer-pricing penalties (10% of gross mispricing) under subsection 247(3) on non-arm's-length cross-border transactions, and absence of FX repatriation within 180 days is treated by auditors as an indicator of unreported foreign revenue or unremitted export proceeds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) – sole monetary authority; Foreign exchange policy is administered by the Department of Finance Canada, with anti-money laundering supervision by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) and currency reporting at borders by the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA). No single foreign exchange control authority exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is a fully convertible currency. Canada has dismantled all exchange controls for both current-account (trade in goods and services, remittances, travel) and capital-account (direct and portfolio investment, borrowing, repatriation) transactions. No administrative approval or central bank consent is required for convertibility. Profit remittances, dividends, management fees, and royalty payments to non-residents are freely transferable, subject solely to standard anti-money laundering, sanctions screening, and beneficial ownership verification by the remitting financial institution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender requirement exists. Canadian law imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement to repatriate export proceeds to Canada within a specific period. Exporters may maintain foreign currency accounts in Canada or abroad; however, any proceeds received in a Canadian account are subject to standard FINTRAC reporting thresholds (e.g., CAD 10,000 equivalent) and must be supported by underlying commercial documents for audit and transfer purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Canada does not legally recognize 'Electronic Money Institutions' as a distinct bank or deposit-taking category. Non-bank fintech payment providers must register as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) with FINTRAC. They may facilitate cross-border payment transmission, FX conversion, and virtual IBAN issuance, but they cannot hold client funds as deposits, cannot issue regulated letters of credit, and are subject to additional provincial licensing under Quebec's Money-Services Businesses Act. Legal constraints: (i) no deposit insurance (CDIC) coverage; (ii) funds must be held in trust accounts at a Canadian Schedule I bank; (iii) no direct access to the Canadian Large Value Transfer System (LVTS); (iv) limited to payment-only instruments. For an export operating entity, use of an MSB is practical for small-value ancillary transfers but not for bulk trade settlements or capital escrow purposes.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person physical presence is generally not mandatory for corporate account opening if the company and its directors are non-resident. Canadian Schedule I banks require enhanced remote onboarding using Notarized Acceptable Evidence of Identity (AEI) documents, certified true copies, and a live-video interview conducted by a compliance officer. However, at least one signing officer or representative (e.g., the sole director) must pass an identity verification and may be required to attend a short on-site or remote video call at the bank's discretion. For Quebec specifically, financial institutions regulated under An Act respecting the distribution of financial products and services may impose a physical presence requirement for high-risk jurisdictions; for a Canada-incorporated trading entity, remote onboarding is accepted if the beneficial owner passes sanctions and PEP screening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner with 100% control of a Canadian entity engaged in cross-border wholesale export
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Resolution of directors authorizing bank signatories; Articles of Incorporation / Certificate of Incorporation; Full beneficial ownership attestation (individuals >25%) with registered address, occupation, and source of wealth; Organization chart showing ultimate parent - intermediate holding - Canadian operating entity; Trade contracts (porforma invoices for goji berry and herbal shipments); Register of directors and any Quebec Register of Enterprises extract; Notarized proof of identity and address for each shareholder and director; Brief written business plan describing product type (dried lycium / herbal botanicals), supply chain, and expected monthly transaction volume and counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency wire transfers to and from China, India, or Vietnam (common goji berry supply origins) without prior banking history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed commercial agreements with overseas suppliers (purchase orders, quality certificates, phytosanitary certificates); Detailed invoices showing unit pricing and shipping terms (Incoterms); Bill of lading / airway bill and customs entry records; Importer / Exporter Program (PEP) or customs broker confirmation; Justification for payment timing and counterparty location relative to the trade flow; For countries with unique sanctions exposure, providing letters from independent auditors confirming no dual-use or controlled-good involvement in any herbal botanical product.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large lump-sum inbound capital injection (e.g., initial shareholder loan or equity contribution) exceeding CAD 500,000
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed shareholder loan agreement or board resolution declaring equity contribution; Foreign exchange source documentation (e.g., bank statement from source jurisdiction showing prior origin of funds); Income tax return / net worth statement of the lending shareholder; Business plan and cash flow projection justifying capital requirements; Statement of no Canadian income yet generated; Notarized promissory note if funds are provided as debt; Compliance report demonstrating that proceeds will be used only for shelter inventory liquidation and working capital, not for securities or real estate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner appears on a politically exposed persons (PEP) or adverse media list
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent verification of all directors and shareholders through a licensed Canadian compliance background-screening tool; Legal opinion from a Canadian securities / banking counsel confirming the beneficial owner's status as a foreign PEP; Declaration of familial, business, or professional relationships to any government entity; For any negative news, a reasoned rebuttal memorandum supported by court filings or public records; Commitment to provide quarterly transaction monitoring and enhanced source-of-funds reporting on request.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for an inbound injection (equity or debt) from a non-resident parent to the Quebec entity must be sent via SWIFT MT103 to the Canadian bank's correspondent account (CAD or USD) under SWIFT field 50K (ordering customer) and field 72 (bank-to-bank information). Recommended purpose codes (ISO 20022 external purpose codes): 'FDIN' for foreign direct investment / equity capital, 'LIQU' for trade-related liquidity support, or 'TRAD' for advance payment on goods. For shareholder loans, use 'LOAN' or 'INTC' (intercompany loan). The remitter should state in field 70 a concise narrative such as 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN / FC INVESTMENT / CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - FOR OPERATING EXPENSES OF DRIED GOJI BERRY SOLUTIONS.' Verification: the receiving bank will perform sanctions screening on all parties, confirm the corporate name of the beneficiary, and may request a copy of the executed shareholder loan or board resolution, applicable Investment Canada Act notification name of ultimate investor, and supporting invoice if the injection is trade-related. Amounts exceeding CAD 10,000 must be reported to FINTRAC under a Large Cash Transaction Report (LCTR), though the report is filed by the bank, and not by the client.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For commercial settlements from the Quebec entity to foreign suppliers and logistics providers, the primary clearing rails are: (1) SWIFT MT103 (direct wire transfer) for open-account, partial prepayments, or final settlement, using purpose code 'GOODS' or 'TRAD', and (2) Documentary Letter of Credit (L/C) via SWIFT MT700, commonly a sight irrevocable L/C confirmed by the seller's bank (for large bulk herbal consignments). For periodic payments like freight and insurance, MT103 with the relevant corporate general purpose code is sufficient. Canada's internal clearing infrastructure (LVTS / Automated Clearing Settlement System) is only for CAD-denominated domestic wires; cross-border outbound flows must use SWIFT. Practical guidance: keep a dedicated foreign-currency denomination (USD or CNY) for trade payments to avoid double conversion; maintain a reserve in the operating account to cover hedging margins; and ensure all outward remittances references include the original invoice number and a cross-reference to the applicable import permit if the destination country requires one.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Canadian dollar / US dollar foreign exchange forwards (plain vanilla FX swaps) – permitted for all non-financial trading corporates without derivatives licensing
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD, CAD/CNY) for long-term purchase price fixed-currency obligations – available from Schedule I banks under an ISDA Master Agreement or a master FX confirm
Over-the-counter options (put and call) on USD/CAD for trade receivable and payable protection – unregulated for commercial hedgers
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted when hedging USD/CNH or exotic currencies due to CNH onshore non-transferability, using the recognized offshore CNH fixing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Updating Declaration (Déclaration de mise à jour)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation or initial registration; every calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty up to C$1,200 plus administrative charges; failure to file for 3 consecutive years triggers administrative dissolution by REQ

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after fiscal year-end (e.g., June 30 for December 31 year-end); filing due irrespective of taxable income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; interest at prescribed CRA rates on unpaid balance; no automatic strike-off but registry actions may follow for persistent non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after fiscal year-end; same fiscal year-end as T2
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty from C$100 plus accrued interest; failure to remit may lead to collection actions and liens; no automatic strike-off but persistent default may escalate to provincial enforcement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CBCA Annual Return (if incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development (ISED) Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of the anniversary of federal incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No monetary penalty, but five consecutive years of failure to file annual returns allows the Director to dissolve the corporation under section 212 of the CBCA

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit for private corporations solely based on size; an auditor must be appointed unless all shareholders waive the audit by unanimous resolution under the Quebec Business Corporations Act or the CBCA. An audit is compulsory for public companies and for corporations subject to specific regulatory requirements (e.g., financial intermediaries). Shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares may requisition a court-ordered audit if they suspect wrongdoing.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Private corporations may elect IFRS or ASPE (Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook); public companies must use IFRS. Quebec corporate tax filings follow CRA/Revenu Québec rules but financial statements may be prepared under either framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (Quebec), the corporation must maintain a register of ultimate beneficiaries and confirm its accuracy annually by filing the updating declaration with REQ. Any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership must be recorded in the register and reflected in the next annual declaration. Federal CBCA corporations must separately file beneficial ownership information with Corporations Canada. Failure to update constitutes an offence and may attract penalties up to C$5,000 for corporations.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$150 – US$480 (C$200 – C$650) per year for a registered office or corporate agent in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,700 – US$11,000 (C$5,000 – C$15,000) if a full audit is required; nil if waived by unanimous shareholder resolution

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for dried goji berry/herbal wholesale. A Canadian-controlled private corporation may claim the federal Small Business Deduction on the first C$500,000 of active business income, reducing the federal rate to 9%; Quebec's small business reduction lowers the provincial rate on eligible income. Qualifying CCPCs therefore pay a combined rate on eligible active business income in the approximate range of 12.2% to 13.5%, depending on the current Quebec rate schedule. SR&ED and investment tax credits are available only for qualifying research, development and innovation activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed electronically through CRA E-file (approved software or CRA Web Forms) and My Business Account; supporting schedules include Schedule 1, 3, 4, 7, 8, 21 and Form T106 for reportable non-arm's-length transactions.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 is due on or before the day that is six months after the end of the taxation year. For a Canadian-controlled private corporation, the federal balance-due date is generally three months after year-end; for other corporations it is generally two months after year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue or sales: wholesale invoice value of organic dried goji berry and herbal botanical export sales, before trade discounts, returns and allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Canadian-source business income attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment. Sales negotiated and completed abroad may remain treaty-protected and should be disclosed on Schedule 21.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Purchases and cost of goods sold: acquisition costs of goji berries, herbal botanicals, packaging, freight, duties and direct production or repackaging expenditures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Substantiate all cross-border inventory purchases with customs entries and contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation when the supplier is related or non-arm's-length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit: reconciliation of revenue to gross margin before operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use benchmark gross margins from comparable wholesale distributors; a lack of economic substance in Canadian operations will invite recharacterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income before taxes and provincial allocation: apportionment of taxable income to Quebec and other provinces under permanent-establishment rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Income is allocated to provinces where the corporation has a permanent establishment; non-residents must use sales and salary attribution factors consistently with the Quebec tax return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Small Business Deduction claim for qualifying active business income up to C$500,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not available to non-resident-controlled or public corporations; foreign corporate shareholders must apply the general 26.5% combined rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Investment tax credits, including SR&ED credits for qualifying botanical/health product research and development.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Canadian-qualified scientific research and experimental development expenditure is creditable; foreign-related R&D cannot be shifted into the Canadian entity merely to generate credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty is 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; repeated failure attracts 10% plus 2% per month up to 20 months. CRA charges daily compound interest on unpaid balances at the prescribed rate. Wilful omissions trigger gross-negligence penalties of 50% of understated tax and, in fraud cases, criminal penalties under section 239 of the Income Tax Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Revenu Québec CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed through Revenu Québec online services (Clic Revenu / COT.RI) or an approved electronic filing service; provincial schedules include the calculation of taxable income, tax credits and the small business deduction.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: CO-17 is due six months after the fiscal year-end. Quebec payment deadlines align with the corporation type: generally the second or third month after year-end for most corporations; installment obligations arise when tax payable exceeds the quarterly threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales and revenues from wholesale trade in dried goji berry and herbal botanicals.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only income allocable to a Quebec permanent establishment; income from a foreign permanent establishment is excluded after treaty application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales and inventory adjustments for agricultural and herbal wholesale inventory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Inventory costs must mirror federal T2 Schedule 1 amounts and respect arm's-length transfer-pricing principles for cross-border related-party purchases.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net business income after deductible operating expenses, freight, insurance, repackaging and export logistics.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses incurred for the Quebec permanent establishment; head-office expense allocations must be documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec small business deduction for eligible active business income up to C$500,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only if the corporation is a Canadian-controlled private corporation and the same income was not subject to the federal small business deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CO-17 Schedule C / relevant tax credit schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec tax credits such as SR&ED, innovation, and e-business credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations may claim only credits for activities physically performed in Quebec and directly connected to the provincial permanent establishment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts 5% of the balance due plus 1% per month up to 12 months; repeated failure attracts 10% plus 2% per month up to 24 months. Daily compound interest accrues at the Revenu Québec prescribed rate, and failure to file instalments incurs separate penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must provide the Canadian payer with a completed Form NR301 (or NR302 for certain connected claims) before the payment date, together with a current Certificate of Residence issued by the treaty jurisdiction's tax authority. The payer may then withhold at the reduced treaty rate. If treaty relief was not claimed at source, the non-resident must apply for a refund using Form NR7-R within the statutory limitation period. A treaty will reduce the 25% statutory Part XIII rate to the applicable rate (commonly 0%, 5%, or 15% for dividends depending on ownership level), but only if the recipient is the beneficial owner and has no permanent establishment in Canada.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory Part XIII rate is 25% for both royalties and interest paid to non-residents. Under most Canadian tax treaties, interest may be reduced to 0% or 10% and industrial/copyright royalties to 0% or 10%, provided the beneficial owner supplies a valid Turkish? No; supplies a valid Certificate of Residence and Form NR301 supporting the treaty claim. Back-to-back or conduit financing structures, excessive management-fee substitution, and payments made to shell entities without economic substance will be recharacterized as dividends subject to 25% Part XIII tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: C$5,000,000 aggregate value of same-nature non-arm's-length cross-border transactions in a taxation year is the practical threshold triggering Canada's contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation expectation and the section 247 penalty; a C$750,000,000 consolidated group revenue threshold triggers Country-by-Country reporting. A formal Local File/Master File is not separately mandated by the Income Tax Act, but CRA and Revenu Québec follow the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines and require complete, contemporaneous and substantiated documentation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not maintain Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations. Instead, economic substance is enforced through the general anti-avoidance rule, the legal sham doctrine, foreign accrual property income rules, and the treaty beneficial-ownership requirement. A Quebec entity that merely invoices dried goji berry exports while holding no inventory, officers, employees, board activity or commercial risk in Quebec is vulnerable to being disregarded for tax purposes, with distributions or invoiced margins recharacterized as taxable Canadian income or Part XIII dividends.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating wholesale revenue, falsifying dried goji berry purchase invoices, manipulating inventory valuation, or maintaining undisclosed offshore bank accounts to evade Canadian and Quebec corporate tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act section 239(1): fine of 50% to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment up to two years; civil gross-negligence penalty under section 163(2) of 50% of the net understatement; Revenu Québec imposes parallel sanctions under the Taxation Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in fraud are jointly and severally liable with the corporation; the corporate veil is pierced and personal assets may be seized. Serious fraud prosecutions may trigger RCMP/Canada Border Services Agency asset freezes, international extradition requests, and travel alerts against non-cooperating director-shareholders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling dried goji berry and herbal botanicals through related offshore procurement entities at marked-up prices without contemporaneous TP documentation, or filing Form T106 inaccurately.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under section 247(3), a penalty of 10% of the net transfer-pricing adjustment applies where the adjustment exceeds the lesser of C$5 million and 10% of gross revenue; interest runs on all reassessed amounts. Recharacterization can convert excessive payments into taxable dividends subject to Part XIII withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who instruct the preparation of sham transfer-pricing policies or knowingly sign false documentation may be assessed personally for gross negligence and, where fraud is established, may face criminal prosecution and personal confiscation orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Quebec business corporation solely as a conduit for dried goji berry export invoices, with no physical presence, staff, inventory or risk-bearing functions in Quebec, and with no documented business purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The CRA and Revenu Québec may apply the GAAR to deny treaty benefits, disregard the entity, and impose tax, interest and penalties on all diverted profits. Beneficial-ownership analysis under tax treaties will disallow reduced withholding rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors and non-resident beneficial owners cannot shelter behind the limited liability shell; courts may pierce the veil, hold directors personally liable for withheld or evaded amounts, impose asset freezes, and issue travel bans where shell funds are moved out of Canada.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, interest or management fees to non-residents without withholding the statutory 25%, without a valid treaty reduction, or while lacking a current foreign Certificate of Residence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Section 215 of the Income Tax Act makes the Canadian payer liable for the full amount that should have been withheld, plus interest and penalties. Revenu Québec may also assess the corporation as agent for the non-resident recipient.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under section 227.1, directors are personally liable for amounts the corporation failed to withhold and remit if the corporation cannot pay. This liability survives corporate wind-up and bankruptcy discharge restrictions apply; CRA cannot be constrained by asset migration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Export Proceeds Red Flags
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving SWIFT/wire payments for herbal exports from counterparties without KYC verification, failing to file a Suspicious Transaction Report, splitting payments to evade reporting thresholds, or falsely declaring commodity values in customs filings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act penalties reach high administrative monetary amounts per violation; Criminal Code money-laundering carries imprisonment up to 14 years; customs false declaration penalties and export permit revocation apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who knowingly execute or direct the unreported wire transfers may be prosecuted personally; conviction may result in personal fines, imprisonment, asset forfeiture, and regulatory bans on acting as directors. Cross-border enforcement can include Interpol travel alerts and extradition.
